Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-medium-0137", "row_sha256": "2a12ca8a7900cc88d03a2a09e4b737a1f3b7789872571fd5b6f4624f32d82744", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help me turn this into a clear request for a short correction for the Northfield Ledger? In Wednesday’s online story about the Maple branch library, we said it is open every Sunday all year. a reader emailed to say the hours change after Labor Day, but nobody here has confirmed that yet. We need to check the library’s official schedule or get confirmation from the branch manager before deciding what to do. if either of those confirms the branch is closed on Sundays after Labor Day, draft a correction saying the story incorrectly described the Sunday hours and that the branch is closed Sundays after Labor Day. don’t make it sound like the branch is closed all year. If the schedule and manager don’t confirm that detail, don’t write or publish a correction and don’t repeat the reader’s claim as fact. instead, give me three concise questions to send to the library so we can verify the Sunday schedule. Keep the request focused on this one factual issue, and don’t add details about other branches, library services, or the reader.", "output": "Draft a short correction for the Northfield Ledger concerning Wednesday’s online story about the Maple branch library, which said the branch is open every Sunday all year.

First, check the library’s official schedule or obtain confirmation from the branch manager. If either source confirms that the branch is closed on Sundays after Labor Day, draft a correction stating that the story incorrectly described the Sunday hours and that the branch is closed Sundays after Labor Day. Do not imply that the branch is closed all year.

If neither source confirms that detail, do not write or publish a correction, and do not present the reader’s claim as fact. Instead, provide three concise questions to send to the library to verify the Sunday schedule.

Keep the request focused on this factual issue. Do not add details about other branches, library services, or the reader."}]
